original_question: If the dual unit ball B_{X^*} is weak*-sequentially compact, must the dual unit ball B_{L^p(μ,X)^*} of the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^p(μ, X) also be weak*-sequentially compact?
target_in_paper: Problem 5.1 in Section 5.1 (Topological properties): “Is B_{L^p(μ,X)^*} w*-sequentially compact if B_{X^*} is?”

refined_question: Let (Ω, Σ, μ) be a probability space, let X be a real Banach space, and let 1 ≤ p < ∞. Write L^p(μ, X) for the Lebesgue-Bochner space of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f: Ω → X such that (∫_Ω ||f(ω)||^p dμ(ω))^(1/p) < ∞. If the closed dual unit ball B_{X^*}, endowed with the weak* topology σ(X^*, X), is weak*-sequentially compact, must the closed dual unit ball B_{L^p(μ,X)^*}, endowed with σ(L^p(μ,X)^*, L^p(μ,X)), also be weak*-sequentially compact?
